The ritual procedure for the worship of the principal goddess who grants all desired objects, consisting of the pacification of activities and so forth based on the *Kālacakra*, preceded by the consecration (*pratiṣṭhā*). [One should worship] the *Kālanityā* daily in both locations: at the site of the *yakṣma* [disease] and at the site of the *Kālacakra* manuscript.

One should worship the principal goddess in the sequence of the wheels; by doing so, Mahālakṣmī shall remain firm throughout his entire lineage. Thus concludes the ritual application for the worship that ensures the stability of Mahālakṣmī. As for the method of constructing the Kālacakra, first:

Having fashioned a circle characterized by great width and possessing a pericarp suitable for the extraction of a single Śrīcakra, one should then delineate sixteen intermediate circles outside that [first] circle, each separated by an interval of one finger-breadth (*aṅgula*), starting from the first circle and ending with the seventeenth circle on the outermost edge.

Having established thirty-six marks for each [of the four directions], one should proceed in order— starting from the first ending in the nominative case and the second ending in the accusative case— from the sixteenth mark beginning with the center, up to the sixteenth mark situated on the outermost perimeter, preceded by the piercing of each respective mark located in the center.
Having cast thirty-six vertical and horizontal lines,
there are thirty-six by thirty-six squares; that is, sixteen squares in each row, both vertically and horizontally.

Having constructed five hundred and seventy-six squares by combining them together, one should write the letters within them; beginning from the foremost square located on the outermost perimeter and proceeding downwards in sequence, one should write the *avarga* group,
and then, following the clockwise order, [place the remaining groups] in descending sequence within the twenty-five rows.

Having written the thirty-six letters beginning with *ka*, each distinguished by the nature of sixteen forms through their sequential connection with the sixteen vowels within the sixteen-by-sixteen grids;
and having written the three-syllable mantra of Kālanityā—*a ā ī*—in the pericarp (*karṇikā*) therein. Therein...

One should write the names of the person to be accomplished (sādhya) and the practitioner (sādhaka), and so forth, within the interior of the fourth vowel; thus is the first annual wheel (varṣacakra) extracted, known as "Anuloma-anuloma" (direct and reverse), according to the sequence. In the second year, in the aforementioned collection of lines (rekhā-samudāya-cakra), starting from the square adjacent to the pericarp (karṇikā) up to the outermost square—
Starting from the outer path (*agravīthī*) and proceeding in a clockwise direction, the thirty-six letters beginning with *a* and ending with the sixteen vowels are written;
having first written the second vowel, which is the form of *ā*, within the pericarp (*karṇikā*) among the colors of the full mandala,
[one proceeds] to the squares reached by moving from the outermost square and the topmost square for the letter *a* to be written.

Having abandoned that [letter] because its syllable is modified, and having joined the first vowel—which is its original form—with the letter *mahat* (the letter *m*), one should write the resulting form *ā*; then, from the second [position], one should write the pure letter *ī*.

As for the drawing of the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*) and the practitioner (*sādhaka*) and so forth within the pericarp (*karṇikā*), it is as before. This is the wheel known as *anuloma-viloma* (direct and reverse).
In the third year of the second [cycle], it consists of the aforementioned collection of lines.
Starting from the foremost outer cell at the top and extending down to the eighth cell below,
one writes the eight vowels beginning with *a*; then, starting from the inner cell connected to that same row,
one writes the vowels beginning with the ninth vowel, which is the form of *lṛ*, up to the sixteenth vowel.

Similarly, in the other rows located to the south as well, one should write the eight syllables beginning with *ka* and ending with *kṛ*, starting from the outermost square; then, in that same row, starting from the innermost square, one should inscribe the syllables beginning with *kḷ* and *kḹ* and ending with *ka*. In the other [rows] as well, [the sequence begins] with the letter *kha*.
The drawing of all the principles (*tatva*) is performed according to the same direction [as previously described]. In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one writes *i*, *ā*, and *ī*;

and in the pericarp, the names of the practitioner (*sādhaka*), the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*), and so forth, are written as before. This wheel, called the "external enclosure in forward order" (*anuloma-vāhya-sampuṭa*), belongs to the third year. In the very wheel mentioned previously, starting from the innermost square on the outer path (*agravīthī*), [the sequence continues].

Starting from the first vowel, one should write the eight vowels in the order of exit; then, starting from the outer square, one should write the ninth and subsequent vowels in the order of entry. Having written "ka, kā, ki, kī," and so forth, in the thirty-five rows proceeding clockwise, beginning from the innermost square in the order of exit, one should again [proceed with] the order of entry.

One should write *kḷ*, *kḹ*, and so forth in sequence. In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), the writing of *ī*, *ā*, *ī*, and the person to be accomplished (*sādhya*) etc., is as before. This is the wheel of the fourth year, known as the "Internal Encasement in Direct Order" (*anulomābhyantara-sampuṭa*). Starting from the eighth square by counting from the outermost corner square, one proceeds in a zigzag manner (*nirjamagati*) with the vowels beginning with *a*.

Having written the eight vowels from *a* to *visarga* on the left [side], one should then write the eight vowels from *a* to *visarga* on the right cheek, beginning from the ninth square and proceeding by the path of entry (*praveśagati*). In this very same manner, it should also be done for the other rows.

Having come from the central square to the outermost square and then returning again, one should place each letter from *ka* to *kṣa* in every square, ending with the innermost square starting from the ninth.

One should inscribe [the syllables] associated with the sixteen vowels. Here, in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), the first is the letter *u*; the second is the letter *ā*, because the first vowel of the nasal class (*nāsāvarṇa*)—though appearing as a modified letter (*vikṛtākṣara*)—is in fact the original letter (*prakṛtyakṣara*), and even when conjoined with the wind (*marut*), it results in being essentially of the nature of the wind; and the third is the letter *ī*. Thus, this is in direct order (*anuloma*).

In the fifth wheel, which is the reversal of the wind, beginning from the ninth square on the central path (agravīthī) and proceeding through all the squares from the outside to the inside, one should write the eight vowels starting with the first vowel (*a*) and ending with the "left nostril" vowel (*au*), and then again—

Having written [the letters] starting from the eighth square and proceeding outward until the outermost square— having written *kḷ* and so forth, ending with *ka*, in the eighth square and continuing to the outermost square—
the remaining thirty-four phonemes representing the *tattvas*, beginning with *kha*, are to be written here according to the previously mentioned method.

In the pericarp (*karṇikā*) is the sixth [vowel], the letter *ū*; according to the previously stated method, it is indeed the first, the second vowel, and likewise the second and third [of that group]. Thus, *ū*, *ā*, *ī*—this is the wheel of the sixth year, known as the "internal reversal in forward order" (*anulomābhyantaraparāvṛtta*). However, if [one considers] the aforementioned wheel itself, within the aforementioned paths (*vīthī*) numbering sixteen, [the sequence is as follows]:

In the first outermost square (p. 23b), there is the letter *a*; in the square located on that same row within the innermost [circle], there is the letter *ā*. In the second [square] from the center, there is the letter *i*, and in the fifteenth [square], there is the letter *ī*.

One should write the letter *ī* in the third [position], *u* in the fourteenth, *ū* in the fourth, *ṛ* in the thirteenth, *ṝ* in the fifth, *ḷ* in the twelfth, *ḹ* in the sixth, *e* in the eleventh, *ai* in the seventh, *o* in the tenth, *au* in the eighth, and *aṃ* in the ninth; thus one should write the letters beginning with *ka*.

Since the sequence is indeed the same even in writing, first the letter *ṛ* is placed in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), then the letter *ā* according to the aforementioned direction, and thirdly the letter *ī*; thus it results in the sequence *ṛ-ā-ī* as that which is to be written. Following this order, there is the seventh annual wheel (*varṣacakra*) called "the externally scattered" (*vāhyavyākīrṇa*). However, if the letter *a* is placed in the innermost square—
In the outermost cell on the right, the letter Ā; in the second, the fifteenth letter I; in the third, the fourteenth letter Ī;
in the fourth, the thirteenth letter U; in the fifth, the twelfth letter Ū; in the sixth, the eleventh letter Ṛ;

in the seventh, the tenth letter Ṝ; in the eighth, the ninth letter Ḷ; in the ninth, the eighth letter Ḹ; in the tenth, the seventh letter E; in the eleventh, the sixth letter AI; in the twelfth, the fifth letter O; and in the thirteenth, the fourth letter AU.
One should write the vowel *au* in the ninth [petal], the vowel *aṃ* in the eighth, and the vowel *aḥ* in the previously mentioned pericarp.
First is the vowel *ṛ*, then the second according to the stated method; thus, it results in *ṝ, ā, ī*.
This is the wheel of the eighth year from the beginning of the Kali Yuga, known as "intermingled with either the forward or reverse order."
These are the eight types of *anuloma* (direct) arrangements.

If, in the very same wheel previously described, the letters beginning with *kṣakṣā* and ending with *kṣakṣaḥ* are written in the order of entry (*praveśagati*) along the outer path (*agravīthī*), starting from the outermost square and ending at the innermost square; [this constitutes another type].

In the internal pathways obtained by moving clockwise, one should write the forms of the thirty-five principles in the shape of sixteen parts, beginning with the letter *ḷ* and ending with the first vowel (*a*).
Here, in the pericarp, first is the syllable *u*, which is another synonym for the right cheek and possesses the color of the full mandala;
then, by the aforementioned method, the second [syllable] is indeed the letter *kṣa* associated with the second vowel; and the third is the fourth vowel itself.

The writing of the *sādhya* and other elements within the interior of the vowels was previously mentioned and should not be forgotten here. This is the ninth-year wheel known as *vilomānuloma* (reverse-regular), because it is formed by taking the letters in reverse order while the squares are taken in regular order. However, if [one uses] this very wheel—

Starting from the innermost square and extending to the outermost square, the thirty-six letters of the principles (*tattva*), beginning with *kṣa* and ending with the first vowel (*a*), are written in all the squares reached by proceeding clockwise, starting from the eastern row; in the pericarp (*karṇikā*) is written *ḷkṣāī*.
The tenth year-wheel, known as *vilomaviloma*, is formed by reversing both the consonant (*avarṇa*) and vowel (*koṣṭha*) grids.
Alternatively, within this very wheel, starting from the outer grid and proceeding through the eight inner grids beginning with the front row,
one places *kṣa kṣā kṣi kṣī kṣu kṣū kṣṛ kṣṝ* and so forth, followed by *a ā i ī u ū ṛ ṝ*.
Having thus written the eight letters ending with *tattattva* by way of entry and progression, one should again write,

starting from the innermost square and proceeding through those same paths, the group of eight letters beginning with *kṣḷ kṣḹ kṣe kṣau kṣaṃ kṣaḥ* and ending with *ḷ ḹ e ai o au aṃ aḥ*, extending up to eight squares in each direction in sequence.

In the pericarp (karṇikā) are *e* and *ī*; thus, this is the eleventh annual wheel, known as the "inverse outer enclosure" (*vilomabāhyasaṃpuṭa*). However, if in this very wheel one writes the eight syllables *kṣa kṣā kṣi kṣu kṣū kṣṛ kṣṝ* by way of exiting from the inner square and so forth, then *aikṣāī* is written in the pericarp.
Then, the twelfth-year wheel known as the *vilomābhyantarasaṃpuṭa* (the inverted inner enclosure) is as follows:
starting from the eighth square in this very same row and so forth, [one proceeds] up to the outermost square. *Kṣa*...

When one has written *kṣā kṣī* and so forth up to the end of the eighth group of syllables beginning with *a ā i ī*, and then, starting from the ninth [cell] and continuing inward through all the inner compartments, has written *kṣḷ kṣḹ kṣe kṣai* and so forth up to the end of the eighth group of syllables beginning with *ḷ ḹ e ai*, and finally writes *o ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), then—

The thirteenth year-wheel is called *vilomavāhyaparānṛtta*. However, if in this very wheel one begins from the ninth square of the outer path (*agravīthī*) and writes the eight syllables starting with *kṣa kṣā kṣi kṣī* up to the innermost square, and then again [the eight syllables] starting with *a ā i ī* and so forth; |||

Having written the group of eight syllables beginning with *kṣḷ kṣḹ kṣe kṣai* from the eighth square outward to the outermost square, and continuing up to the group of eight syllables beginning with *ḷ ḹ e ai*, one then writes *au ī* in the pericarp; this constitutes the fourteenth-year wheel known as the "reversal from the inside in reverse order."
If, in this very wheel, the letters *bhū-bhū-pada* are the guest (the thirteenth), and *vahni-surādhinātha-brahmāsya* (three, twelve,

the letters beginning with *kṣa-kṣā* follow in sequence in the first row, while those beginning with *la* appear in the other rows.
By this same method of writing according to the sequence ending with the first vowel, if one writes *aṃ* and *ī* here within the pericarp (*karṇikā*) as the objects of the action,

then it becomes the fifteen-year wheel (*pañcadaśavarṣacakra*) known as "scattered in reverse order" (*vilomabāhyakīrṇa*). However, if in this very line-drawn wheel (*rekhāmayacakra*), starting from this square (*koṣṭha*), [the letters are placed] in the squares numbered by the earth (1), the moon (1), the lunar days (15), the stars (7), and the gods (3) [respectively]...

In the thirteenth [row], starting from the single *veda* (4), the *ekaiṣayaka* (13), the *ekadra* (1), the *ṣaṣṭha* (6), the *akhaka* (0), and the *naga* (8), the letters beginning with *kṣa* and *kṣā* follow in sequence until the letter *ṛ*. The sixteen measures (*unmāna*) are written in the pericarp (*karṇikā*) through their conjunction with the sixteen vowels: *aḥ* and *ī*. These are the eight varieties of the reverse-order wheels (*vilomacakrabheda*). Within this very wheel, on the outer path (*agravīthī*),...
The sixteen forms of the first vowel, differentiated by the sixteen vowels and transformed into the very nature of those respective vowels—

Having written, in a clockwise sequence within the seventeen internal lanes, sixteen forms for each of the seventeen phonemes representing the principles (tattvas) from *ka* to *tha*—

The wheel of seventeen syllables, known as the "outer enclosure in forward order," has been extracted. Alternatively,
within this very wheel, starting from the outermost corner cell and proceeding by way of exit toward the innermost corner cell,

Having written eight groups of eight letters for each of the vowels, starting from the outer square up to the eighth square of the eighth [set], those respective second groups are written in an outward direction, ending at the ninth inner square. Due to the external encapsulation (*vāhyataḥpuṭīkaraṇāt*), there arises the nineteenth-year wheel known as the "External Encasement" (*bāhyasaṃpuṭa*).

If, however, in this very same wheel, starting from the central row (*agravīthī*) and proceeding through the eighteen rows, one places the vowels beginning with the first vowel (*prathamasvara*) in each row within the eight squares beginning with the innermost square;

Having first written the eight primary forms, *kṣa*, *kṣā*, *kṣi*, *kṣī*, and so forth, inside [the grid], one should again write them outside, ending with the eighth cell of each of the eight [rows].

Having written the second forms of the vowels—*ḷ*, *ḹ*, *e*, *ai*, and so forth—ending with the forms *tho*, *thau*, *thaṃ*, and *tha*;

and having written the remaining primary forms of the consonants from *kṣa* to *da* in the outer rows, starting from the eighth-eighth squares up to the exterior; then, turning back again, [one writes] starting from the innermost square.

The letters *ku*, *ā*, and *ī* are written in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). Thus, this is the twenty-first-year wheel known as the "outer reversal" (*vāhyasaṃpuṭavāhyaparāvṛtta*), beginning from the innermost square and ending with the ninth square.
However, if in this very wheel [the sequence proceeds] from the innermost square up to the ninth square...

The second pair of eights is written from the outside, ending at the eighth square of the eighth [layer]. In the pericarp are *kū*, *ā*, and *ī*; thus, this is the twenty-second-year wheel, known as the "outer enclosure with internal reversal. If, however, in this very wheel...

The writing of the eighteen vowels from *a* to *au*: having established [the grid] in squares numbered by earth (1), king (16), arm (2), lunar day (15), fire (3), Indra (14), Veda (4), Viśva (13), arrow (5), sun (12), taste (6), Śiva (11), mountain (7), row (10), elephant (8), and Nanda (9); and having likewise placed the phonemes of the principles from *kṣa* to *da* in the subsequent eighteen channels. Earth, king... [repeated].

If one were to write them in sequence: *kṛ*, *ā*, *ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), then this is the twenty-third year-wheel, known as the "Outer Encasement" (*bāhyasaṃpuṭa*) and the "External Scattered" (*bāhyavyākīrṇa*). Or else, in this very wheel, [the letters are placed] in the squares corresponding to the earth (1), the elements (5), the lunar days (15), the asterisms (27), Indra (14) and Agni (3), Viśve (13) and Vedas (4), Sūrya (12) and Bāṇa (5), and Śiva (11) and Rasa (6).

Having written the sixteen syllables beginning with the first, second, and third [of the series], as well as the sixteen vowels, in the eighteen rows of the Paṅkti and Parvata [sections] and likewise in the eight [rows] of Ānanda, in their respective order; and having written the first eighteen [syllables] of the Svasyaugaja [section] in the [corresponding] rows.

Immediately thereafter, having written the letters of the principles (*tattva*) beginning with *ka* and ending with *da* within the eighteen rows (*vīthī*), according to the directions specified by the rule "in the earths, lunar days, and asterisms," one should write *kṛ*, *ā*, and *ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
This constitutes the twenty-fourth year-wheel, known as the "externally encapsulated, internally interspersed" (*bāhya-sampuṭābhyantara-vyākīrṇa*); these are the eight [syllables].
The external combinations and divisions.

In this very wheel, on the foremost path itself, from the outside toward the end of the inner square, having written the sixteen forms of the letter *da*— namely *da, dā, di, dī, du, dū, dṛ, dṝ, dḷ, dḹ, de, dai, do, dau, daṃ, daḥ*— one proceeds clockwise through the remaining seventeen paths to write the seventeen syllables beginning with *bha* and ending with *kṣa*.

Having drawn the sixteen forms, [one should place] the sixteen forms obtained according to the previous method for the eighteen syllables of the principles (*tattva*) beginning with *tha* and ending with *ka*, within the eighteen paths (*vīthī*) reached by proceeding in a clockwise direction. *Tha*... One should write the letters beginning with *tha*, *thi*, *thī*, *kṣa*, *pā*, and so on, ending with *o*, *au*, *aṃ*, and *aḥ*, in the manner of entry (*praveśagatyā*). In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), the sequence beginning with *ḍḷ*, *dā*, and *ī*—that is, the entire series—is to be written throughout the sixteen days of each [period] up to the thirty-sixth day.
This constitutes the twenty-fifth-year wheel, known as the "Internal Encasement in Direct Order" (*ābhyantarasaṃpuṭānuloma*).
In this very wheel, within the *agravīthī* (foremost path) and the others, in sequence from the inner square to the outer square,
the sixteen forms of the eighteen letters beginning with *da* and ending with *kṣa*, as previously described, are to be written;
and in the subsequent paths (*vīthīs*), the sixteen forms of the elemental letters (*tatvākṣara*) beginning with *tha* and ending with *ka* are to be written in sequence.
They are written as follows: in the pericarp (*karṇikā*) and everywhere else, one should write *kḷvā* and *ī*.

This is the twenty-sixth year-wheel, known as the "inner inverted casket" (*abhyantara-sampuṭa-viloma*). In this very wheel, beginning from the foremost outer square up to the eighth square, [the letters] beginning with *da* [are to be placed].

Having first inscribed the eighteen syllables of the principles ending with the letter *kṣa*, each differentiated by the eight vowels beginning with *a*, starting from the innermost square and ending with the ninth square;

then, in the remaining eighteen rows, [one writes] the letters of the principles starting from *tha* up to the first vowel (*a*).

One should first write the eight initial forms in an outward-going direction starting from the very center, and then again in an inward-going direction starting from the very periphery. One should write "kai dā ī" in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
This is the twenty-eighth year-wheel, known as the "inner casket within a casket."
It is as follows: if, within this very wheel,

beginning from every eighth square and proceeding in an outward direction until the end of the outermost square, one writes the forms of the phonemes of the principles (tattva) starting with *da* and ending with *kṣa*, differentiated by the first eight vowels;

From the ninth square up to the end of all the innermost squares, the forms of those very same principles (*tattvas*), differentiated by the vowels beginning with the ninth, are written in the manner of entry; likewise,
in the remaining eighteen paths (*vīthīs*), the eight-by-eight forms of the principles beginning with *pa* and ending with the first vowel are written.
Starting from the first and eighth square, one should write by way of exiting;

then, starting from the ninth square, one should write by way of entering. In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should write "Ko Dā Ī" on all days alike. Thus, this is the twenty-ninth-year wheel, known as the "inner casket with external reversal."

It is as follows: in this very wheel, having first written the forms of the phonemes of the principles (*tattva*) beginning with *da* and ending with *kṣa*, each differentiated by the vowels beginning with *a*, starting from the innermost part up to the ninth enclosure;
and then, having written them again from the outer enclosure up to the eighth enclosure, beginning with the letter *tha*.

One should first write the eighteen syllables ending with the first vowel from the inner side up to the ninth [square], and then from the outer side up to the eighth [square] in the nineteen remaining rows. (p.

In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), [the syllables] *kau* and *dāī* occur everywhere; this is that thirtieth-year wheel called the "internal reversal within the internal casket" (*ābhyantara-sampuṭābhyantara-parāvṛtta*). Having written the sixteen forms in the rows starting from the earth [square] in sequence— beginning with "ṣoḍaśarūpāṇyavatsiṣṭapaṅktiṣu bhūmiṣoḍaśa" and so forth— and having written the three-syllabled vidyā "kaṃ dā ī" in the pericarp (karṇikā),
this becomes the thirty-first year-wheel, known as the "inner casket," "outer," and "scattered."

If, however, within this very wheel, each of the phonemes of the principles (tattva) from *a* to *kṣa* is differentiated by the sixteen vowels, there arise in total two hundred and eighty-eight forms. These are located on the earth,
first in Viśikha-Kaulocana, and in the fire of the Lord of the Immortals (Agni).
In the diagram, having correctly written [the letters] in sequence upon eighteen rows of the remaining paths— starting from the letter *tha* and ending with the vowels,

each divided by the sixteen vowels and measuring eight, one, eight, and two [units] respectively— in the squares for the Sun, the Moon, the Day-maker (Sun), the Arrow (Fire), the Moon, the Water (Varuṇa), the Earth, and the Mountain (Meru), as well as in the squares for Nanda and Kuñjara.
All the pericarp petals, however, consist of the syllables *ka*, *dā*, and *ī*;
thus, this is the thirty-second annual wheel, known as the "interspersed within the inner enclosure.
In this manner, the eight divisions of the inner enclosure have been described.

In the aforementioned line-diagram (*rekhāmaya-cakra*), within the front path (*agravīthī*) and so forth, there are sixteen variations for each of the eighteen principles (*tattva*)—beginning with *tha* and ending with the first vowel (*a*)—arranged in reverse order.
Having written the sixteen forms of each group, beginning with *tha tha thi thī* and so forth, starting from the outermost square and proceeding by way of entry until the innermost square,
one should then place greed (*lobha*) in the remaining nineteen and other subsequent rows in due order, within those [letters] beginning with *da* and ending with *kṣa*.

Having written the sixteen forms of each of the eighteen principles (tattvas) that follow in sequence, starting from the outermost square and proceeding inward toward the center, one should write *kha*, *thā*, and *ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
This is the thirty-second-year wheel, known as the "External Reversal in Direct Order" (*bāhyaparāvṛttānuloma*).

If, however, in this very wheel, on the foremost path (agravīthī), one begins from the innermost square and writes the forms of the letters starting with *tha* and ending with *kha*— each differentiated by the sixteen vowels— in a clockwise direction, and then [continues] on the nineteenth and subsequent paths...

One should write the sixteen forms of the eighteen phonemes of the principles (*tattva*), beginning with the letter *da* and ending with the letter *kṣa*, starting from the innermost square and extending to the outermost square. In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should write *khā*, *thā*, and *ī*.
This is the thirty-fourth year-wheel, known as the "external reversal in reverse order" (*vāhyaparāvṛttaviloma*).
In this very wheel,
beginning from the central path (agravīthī), one should write the eight forms of the eighteen letters starting with *tha* and ending with *kṣa*—
namely, *tha*, *thā*, *ti*, *thī*, and so forth— starting from the outer square and continuing up to the eighth square.

However, if within this very wheel, beginning from the eighth square up to the outermost square, one writes the first eight forms of the eighteen elemental syllables starting with *tha* and ending with *ka*;

This constitutes the forty-first annual wheel (*varṣacakra*), which is inwardly transformed and follows the natural order.

However, within this very wheel, from the letter *kṣa* to the letter *da*, there are eighteen elemental syllables; each of these possesses sixteen forms differentiated by the sixteen vowels, [arranged] from the innermost part to the outermost edge.

Having written [the syllables] in an outward-moving sequence, the eighteen letters of the principles (*tattva*) beginning with the first vowel and ending with *tha*, each differentiated by the sixteen vowels, are to be written in the nineteen and subsequent rows, starting from the innermost circle and extending to the outermost square. And in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), [the syllables] *ra-k-ṣ-ā-ī* are written.
Then there is the forty-second year-wheel, known as the "Internal Reversal" (*ābhyantaraparāvṛtti-viloma*).
However, in this very wheel, one should arrange the eighteen syllables beginning with *kṣa* and ending with *da*,
differentiated by the first and first eight vowels respectively, starting from the outer square up to the eighth square.
Having written [it],
and having again written it from the exit of the inner square up to the end of the ninth square by way of the path of departure;
Having again written [the letters] from *a* to *tha*,
one should write the initial forms of the eighteen elemental syllables— which are differentiated by the nine and the first eight vowels— outside, ending within the eighth square.

Furthermore, one should write [the syllables] from nineteen onwards in the rows up to the ninth inner square. In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one writes *khe*, *kṣā*, and *ī*. Thus, this becomes the forty-third-year wheel, known as the "inner-reversal outer-encasement" (*ābhyantaraparāvṛttabāhyasaṃpuṭa*). And if, in this very wheel...

Having written the forms of each of the eighteen consonantal syllables from *kṣa* to *da*, differentiated by the first eight vowels, within the innermost section ending with the ninth square; and having written the forms of those same syllables, differentiated by the [last] eight vowels starting from the ninth, within the outermost section ending with the eighth square.

Having written [the syllables], one should write the first eight forms in the twenty-one lines and so forth by way of outward progression from the inside, and the second eight forms by way of inward progression from the outside; then, one should write *khai kṣā ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This is called the "inner reversal" (*ābhyantaraparāvṛtta*) or "inner casket" (*abhyantarasampuṭa*).
The forty-fourth year-wheel occurs. In this very wheel,

having written the first eight forms of the eighteen elemental syllables beginning with *kṣa* and ending with *da*— starting from the eighth square— in a clockwise direction (*nirgamagatyā*), and then [writing them] again starting from the ninth square in a counter-clockwise direction (*praveśagatyā*).
One should write the two forms of each of the eight [consonants] up to the very end of the innermost square.

Likewise, in the nineteen and subsequent paths, there are also the two forms of the eighteen elemental syllables beginning with *a* and ending with *tha*. This is done first by the outward-moving sequence of the first, eighth, and so on, and subsequently by the inward-moving sequence of the ninth, tenth, and so on.
One should write:
on the pericarp (karṇikā), [the syllables] *kho*, *kṣā*, and *ī*; then, this is called the "inner reversal and outer enclosure" (*ābhyantaraparāvṛttabāhyasaṃpuṭa*).
The forty-fifth year-wheel occurs.
Now, within this very wheel, among the sixteen forms of the eighteen elemental syllables beginning with *kṣa* and ending with *da*,
the first eight forms [are to be placed] starting from the ninth square up to the innermost square.
Having written [the first set] by way of entry, one should again write the second set of eight forms by way of exit, starting from the eighth square up to all the outermost squares; likewise,
in the remaining rows, one should write the first eight forms of the eighteen elemental syllables beginning with *a* and ending with *tha*.
Having written [the syllables] by way of entry from the ninth [petal] and by way of exit from the eighth [petal], which is multiplied by two and eight forms,

one should write *kha*, *au*, *kṣā*, and *ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). Then this becomes the forty-sixth annual wheel, known as the "inner inverted inner-enclosure" (*ābhyantara-parāvṛttābhyantara-sampuṭa*).

If, however, within this very wheel, the sixteen forms of each of the eighteen elemental syllables beginning with *kṣa* and ending with *da* are [placed] in the eighteen paths starting from the front— in the first, the sixteenth, the last,
the fifteenth, the third, the one called Maranātha, the fourth, the one reckoned as Viśva, and the fifth, the one numbered as Dinakṛt— then...
Then, having written the sixteen forms of the eighteen Tattva-syllables from *a* to *tha* in the sixth, seventh, tenth, eighth, and ninth squares,
one should write them in the remaining eighteen rows according to the sequence: first, sixteenth, second, fifteenth, and so forth.
One should write "khaṃ," "kṣā," and "ī" in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
Then this becomes the forty-seventh year-wheel, known as the "inner-revolution-and-outer-scattering" (*ābhyantaraparāvṛttabāhyavyākīrṇa*). If, however, [the practice] is performed in this very wheel:
p.
31b) Then, on the sixteenth, the first, and subsequently the tenth; then on the fourteenth, the third, and the twelfth as the standard;
on the eleventh, the fifth, the eleven, and the sixth; on the tenth, the seventh, the ninth, and then the eighth.
In this manner, having written the sixteen forms of the eighteen elemental syllables beginning with *kṣa* and ending with *da*,
one should again write the sixteen forms of the eighteen elemental syllables beginning with the first vowel and ending with *tha* within the nineteenth and subsequent rows.
Having written [the syllables] in the manner beginning with "in the sixteenth" and "in the first," one should write *khaḥ*, *kṣā*, and *ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).

This constitutes the forty-eighth-year wheel, known as the "inner reversal" (*ābhyantaraparāvṛtta*) and the "inner scattering" (*abhyantaravyākīrṇa*). Thus, the eight varieties of the inner reversal have been described.

However, within this very wheel, the sixteen forms of each of the thirty-six principles (*tattva*)— which are comprised in the sequence *akṣa, kala, kha, ha, ga, sa, gha, ṣa, ṅa, śa, ca, va, cha, la, ja, ra, jha, ya, ña, ma, ṭa, bha, ṭha, va, ḍa, pha, ḍha, pa, ṇa, na, ta, dha, tha, de, ti*— are [to be arranged] from the outer square to the innermost square.
Having written [the letters], one should write *ga*, *ā*, and *ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
This, then, is the forty-ninth year-wheel, known as the "External Scattered in Direct Order" (*bāhyavyākīrṇānuloma*).
However, if within this very wheel, according to the previous method, there are sixteen forms for each of the thirty-six principles (*tattvas*), [then it is different].
One should write [the letters] starting from the innermost square up to the outermost square; in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), one should write *gā* and *ā ī*.
This is the fiftieth-year wheel, known as the "externally scattered in reverse order" (*bāhyavyākīrṇaviloma*).
If, in this very wheel, for each of the thirty-six principles (*tattvas*) beginning with *akṣakala* and *khaha*...
Having written the sixteen forms and so forth, up to the eight forms, starting from the outer square and ending with the eighth square;
and having written the second set of eight-eight forms, starting from the innermost square and ending with the ninth square.
And one should inscribe the three-syllable vidyā—*gi*, *ā*, *ī*—within the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
This is the fifty-first year-wheel, known as the "outer-scattered" (*bāhyavyākīrṇa*) and "outer-casket" (*bāhyasaṃpuṭa*).
In this very wheel, if within those same thirty-six paths (*vīthī*), beginning from the foremost [path] and so forth, those very [elements] such as the vowels (*akṣa*) and the digits (*kalā*)...

Of the thirty-six letters of the *tattvas*, one should write the first eight forms in their respective sixteen-fold forms differentiated by the sixteen vowels; beginning from the innermost square and proceeding in a clockwise direction, these are written in the nine squares, while the remaining eight forms begin from the ninth square.

Having written from the outer square to the end of the eighth square, one should inscribe the three-syllable vidyā "gī ā ī" in the pericarp. This is the fifty-second year-wheel, known as the "Outer-Scattered-Inner-Reversed."

If, however, within this very wheel, in those same thirty-six rows beginning with the first, one writes the first forms of each of the thirty-six letters of the principles (tattvas) beginning with *akṣakalā*— starting from the eighth square of the eighth row up to the outermost square— then...
Having written the second and second [sets of] eight forms starting from the ninth square up to the innermost square,
one should inscribe the three-syllable vidyā— *gu ā ī*— in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
This is the fifty-third year-wheel, known as the "External-Scattered-Internal-Reversed."
However, if within this very wheel, on those same paths beginning with the *agravīthī*, one writes the first eight forms of those very thirty-six principles (*tattva*) and syllables—
beginning from the ninth square and proceeding inward until the innermost square— in the manner of an entry-path;
Having written all eight forms in a counter-clockwise direction, starting from the eighth square and ending with the innermost square,
one should inscribe the three-syllable mantra *gū ā ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This, then, is it.
The fifty-fourth year-wheel is called the "externally scattered and internally transformed.
If, however, within this very wheel, upon those same paths beginning with the *agrā*, there are sixteen forms for each of those thirty-six principles, such as the *akṣakalā*s and so forth.

Having inscribed [the syllables] in sequence in the first, sixteenth, second, fifteenth, third, fourteenth, fourth, thirteenth, fifth, twelfth, sixth, eleventh, seventh, tenth, and eighth-ninth squares, one should also write the three-syllabled mantra "gṛ ā ī" and the *Kālavidyā* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This is as follows:
The fifty-fifth is called the "External Intermixed" (bāhyavyākīrṇa). However, in this very wheel,

within all the paths beginning with the "spokes" (agra), there are sixteen forms for each of those same thirty-six principles (tattva) and syllables— consisting of the vowels and so forth— which are differentiated by the sixteen vowels.

Having written [the syllables] in the sequence of the sixteenth, first, fifteenth, second, fourteenth, third, thirteenth, fourth, twelfth, fifth, eleventh, sixth, tenth, seventh, eighth, and ninth squares, one should inscribe the three-syllabled *Kālanityā* mantra— *gṛ ā ī*— in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This is as follows:

The fifty-sixth year-wheel is known as the "externally scattered" (*bāhyavyākīrṇa*) and the "internally scattered" (*abhyantaravyākīrṇa*). Among these, the eight divisions of the externally scattered have been described. Now, in this very wheel, on the foremost path (*agravīthī*), there are sixteen forms of the letter *kṣa*, beginning with *kṣa*, *kṣā*, *kṣi*, *kṣī*, and so forth.
Having written [the letters] in sequence from all the outer compartments to the innermost compartment,
one proceeds clockwise through the thirty-five subsequent rows: *a*, *la*, *ka*, *ha*, *kha*, *sa*, *ga*, *ṣa*, *gha*, *śa*, *ṅa*.

Furthermore, the sixteen forms of the thirty-five syllables of the *tattvas*—namely *va, ca, jña, cha, ra, ja, ya, jha, ma, ña, bha, ṭa, va, ṭha, pha, ṅa, pa, ḍha, na, ṇa, dha, ta, tha, ti*—are written in their prescribed order. In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), the three-syllable *vidyā*, *gḷ ā ī*, is written; this is known as the "interiorly interspersed in direct order" (*tadabhyantaravyākīrṇānuloma*).

This is the fifty-seventh wheel of the year. Now, within this very wheel, the sixteen forms of the thirty-six *tattva* syllables— consisting of the letter *kṣa*, the first vowel [a], and the letters *la*, *ka*, *ha*, and so forth, arranged in both direct and reverse order— are placed from the innermost square to the outermost square.
They are written in sequence, and in the pericarp (karṇikā), the three-syllable mantra *gḷ kṣā ī* is written.
This constitutes the fifty-eighth year-wheel, known as the "interspersed" (*vyākīrṇa*) and "reverse" (*viloma*) inner [wheel].
However, if in this very wheel, the syllables obtained through the aforementioned method by means of both direct and reverse order—

One should write the first eight forms of all the *tattva*-goddesses starting from the front across the thirty-six rows, ending at the eighth square on the outside, and then writing again from the inside ending at the ninth square; there,
one should inscribe the three-syllable mantra *ge kṣā ī*.
Thus, this is the fifty-ninth year-cycle, known as the "interior-intermingled-exterior-casket" (*ābhyantaravyākīrṇabāhyasaṃpuṭa*).

However, if within these very same paths one were to arrange the forms of those same thirty-six principles— taken in both direct and reverse order— in groups of eight, [it would constitute another cycle].
Having first written from the innermost square up to the ninth square,

and having written the remaining eight squares starting from the outermost square, one should write "gai kṣā ī" in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This is that sixty-year wheel known as the "interior-interior mixed casket" (*abhyantaravyākīrṇābhyantara-sampuṭa*).
It occurs as follows: if, within this very wheel, in those same rows, of those very same scattered syllables—

Having written the first eight forms starting from the eighth square up to the outermost square by way of exiting, and having written [the remaining forms] starting from the ninth square up to the innermost square by way of entering, one should inscribe the three-syllable mantra *gokṣārī* in the pericarp.
Thus, this constitutes the sixty-first wheel of years, known as the "interior-intermingled-exterior-reversed.

However, if within this very wheel, upon those same paths beginning with the front [path], one were to place the first eight forms of those same intermingled syllables— starting from the ninth square up to the innermost square— then...

Having written [the syllables] by way of entry, and having written the second set of eight forms from the eighth square to the end of all the outer squares by way of exit, one should write the three-syllable mantra *gau kṣā ī* in the pericarp. Thus, this becomes the sixty-second annual wheel, known as the "Internal Rotation."

If, however, within this very wheel, in these same rows beginning with the front (agra), those very syllables of the scattered principles are each sixteen-fold in form: in the first sixteen, in the fifth, the twelfth, and the fifteenth;
likewise in the third, the one called Amaranātha, the fourth, the one reckoned as Viśva, and the fifth, the one belonging to Tīkṣṇabhānu.
Then, having placed [the syllables] in the sixth, eleventh, seventh, tenth, and likewise the well-measured eighth square,
one should write "gaṃ," "kṣā," and "ī" in the pericarp.
Thus, this becomes the sixty-third year-wheel, known as the "interior-intermingled" and "exterior-intermingled."
If, however, by means of this very wheel, within its own paths beginning with the tip [of the spokes], those same sixteen forms of those very scattered syllables [are to be found].
In the sixteenth, first, fifth,
fourteenth, third, twenty-first, fourth, twelfth, fifth, ninth, sixth, tenth, seventh, and eighth squares, having placed [the letters], one should write "gaḥ", "kṣā", and "ī" in the pericarp.

Thus, this is the sixty-fourth year-cycle of the respective yuga, known as the "interior-intermingled" (*ābhyantaravyākīrṇa*). These eight divisions of the interior-intermingled have been described. Thus, the supreme reality has been explained according to the *Āṣṭaka*.
Just as in the first *aṣṭaka*, the fourth *aṣṭaka* follows the sequence beginning with the letter *da*; in the fifth, the sequence begins with *tha*;

and following this pattern up to the eighth *aṣṭaka*, which begins with the sequence starting from *kṣa*, the thirty-six letters representing the *tattvas* should, in my view, be written in every instance within the central portion, ending on the sixteenth day for each group of sixteen.

By this much, the sixty-four divisions of the circular *kālacakra* have been demonstrated; in the same way, the sixty-four divisions of the thirty-six-pointed *kālacakra* are also to be inferred. The distinction therein is as follows: having first made a circle as before at the very center, [one should draw] lines attached to it with equal intervals.

Having made thirty-six marks, and having produced thirty-six corners by drawing lines in the shape of the letter *jva* from each preceding mark to the next successive mark, and having made sixteen circular intervals outside of that, each separated by an interval of one finger-breadth (*aṅgula*). Therein:
Having drawn thirty-six marks consisting of circles located at all internal and external points,
and having laid down sixteen lines starting from the innermost mark and ending at the outermost mark,
The Kālacakra, consisting of five hundred and seventy-six squares and thirty-six corners, is entirely arisen.

Among those, nothing at all is to be written in the thirty corners; however, in its pericarp, there are first sixteen forms of the *gha*-group, beginning with *gha*, *ghā*, *ghi*, *ghī*, and so forth.

From the sixty-fifth year up to the eightieth year, there are the forms of the *eka-śa* (single-consonant) class. Then, until the ninety-sixth year, there are the sixteen forms of the *ṅa*-class, beginning with *ṅa*, *ṅā*, *ṅi*, *ṅī*, and so forth.
After that, until the one hundred and twelfth year, there are the forms of the *ca*-class.
Then, for a period of one hundred and twenty-eight years, sixteen forms of the *cha*-group (*chavarga*) are to be written.

As for the second group of letters (*varṇas*), they are divided by means of the same rules as before, through the distinction of eight-year and eight-year periods. The third group, however, follows the same pattern in every respect. The letters of the *vīthī* likewise arise from that very same method, neither less nor more.

The object of meditation: The eighteen-spoked Wheel of Time (*kālacakra*) is also to be understood according to the aforementioned method; the first syllable [is to be applied] across the sixty-four years, beginning from the one hundred and twenty-ninth year up to the one hundred and ninety-second year.
Successively, for each of the letters beginning with *ja*, there are sixteen forms; the remainder is as before.
The twelve-spoked Kālacakra has been largely extracted. In its pericarp is the first syllable;

among the sixty-four years, starting from the two hundred and fifty-sixth year and continuing sequentially from the one hundred and ninety-third year, there is a single [instance] each of the phonemes *ṭha*, *ḍa*, *ḍha*, and *ṇa*.
There are sixteen forms for each of the sixteen; the remainder is entirely as before.
The *Navakīrṇaka-kālacakra* is also largely extracted [here]. In that [work], within the pericarp (*karṇikā*),
starting from the year two hundred and fifty-seventh (257) of the first syllable up until the three hundred and twentieth (320) year:

In sixty-four years, there are sixteen forms each for the four castes (*catur-varṇa*) consisting of *ta*, *tha*, *da*, and *dha*; the rest is as previously stated. Next, the eight-cornered wheel of time (*kālacakra*) is drawn; first, a single circle is raised.

Having made eight marks there and drawn a horizontal line in the shape of a bowstring from one mark to another, thus forming eight corners; and having established thirty-six concentric circles outside of that, each separated by an interval of one finger-breadth (aṅgula). Therein—
Having marked sixteen points each on both the innermost and outermost circles,
one proceeds as before,
joining the first with the first, the second with the second, the third with the third, and so forth, up to the sixteenth with the sixteenth.
Having produced sixteen paths by drawing lines between the innermost and outermost marks up to the end of the dark sign,
one obtains a wheel of sixty-four squares (576) consisting of sixteen paths,
with thirty-six squares per path. Having extracted the Kālacakra from there, the method for placing the syllables therein is as follows:

For example: here, in this outermost path consisting of thirty-six squares, beginning from the first square and proceeding clockwise by way of entry until reaching the innermost square, one places [the letters] *a, ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa* in the thirty-six squares.

Having written the first forms of the thirty-six *tattva*-syllables, beginning with *ca* and ending with *halakṣa*, which are connected to the first vowel (*a*)— namely *a, ka, kha, ga*, and so on— in a clockwise sequence, one proceeds through the fifteen subsequent paths (*vīthīs*), starting from the second path immediately following each, in regular order.

Each of these is individually joined with the fifteen vowels from the second vowel (*i*) up to the visarga (*ḥ*): beginning with *ā kā khā gā ghā ṅā ca*, and so forth, ending with *hālākṣā*; and beginning with *i ki khi gi ghi ṅi cī*, and so forth, ending with *hilikṣī*.
*ī kī khī gī ghī ṅī cī* and so forth, ending with *hī lī kṣī*; *u ku khu gu ghu ṅu cu* and so forth, ending with *hulukṣu*;
*ū kū khū gū ghū ṅū cū* and so forth, ending with *hū lū kṣū*; *ṛ kṛ khṛ gṛ ghṛ ṅṛ cṛ* and so forth, ending with *hṛ ḷ kṣṛ*; *ṝ kṝ khṝ gṝ ghṝ ṅṝ cṝ* and so forth, ending with *hṝ ḹ kṣṝ*.

...ending with *l*. [The series] beginning with *ḷ kḷ khḷ gḷ ghḷ ṅḷ cḷ* and ending with *hḷ lḷ kṣḷ*; beginning with *ḹ kḹ khḹ gḹ ghḹ ṅḹ cḹ* and ending with *hḷ ḹ kṣḹ*; beginning with *e ke khe ge ghe ṅe ce* and ending with *he le kṣe*; beginning with *ai kai khai gai ghai ṅai cai* and ending with *ni hai lai kṣai*; [and] *o ko kho go gho ṅo*.
The series beginning with *ca* and ending with *ho lo kṣo*; the series beginning with *au kau khau gau ghau ṅau cau* and ending with *hau lau kṣau*;
the series beginning with *aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ* and ending with *haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ*; and the series beginning with *aḥ kaḥ khaḥ gaḥ ghaḥ ṅaḥ caḥ* and ending with *haḥ laḥ kṣaḥ*.

Having written the thirty-six syllables of the thirty-six principles, one should inscribe the three-syllable vidyā— *na*, *ā*, *ī*— in the pericarp. This constitutes the twenty-first year-wheel of the eight-cornered Kālacakra, known as the "direct and reverse" (*lomānuloma*) of the mantras.
If, however, these very same syllables are written here in the wheel itself, starting from the innermost square in the east and proceeding to the outermost square,
letter by letter along every row and every cell, and the three-syllable sequence *nāṃ kṣā ī* is written in the pericarp (*karṇikā*),
then it becomes the 322nd year-wheel known as *anuloma-viloma*. Herein—

Since the letter *kṣa* occupies the foremost square, the letter of the wind (*marut*) associated with it alone is entitled to attain the status of the second letter; provided that, in this very wheel, one begins from the square of *vā*.

Having written the eighteen syllables representing the eighteen principles— ka, kha, ga, gha, ṅa, ca, cha, ja, jha, ña, ṭa, ṭha, ḍa, ḍha, ṇa, ta, tha, and da— in a clockwise direction within the eighteen squares; then, from the very center up to the nineteenth square, [the letters] da, dha, na, and so forth.
Having written the eighteen syllables ending with *kṣa* by way of outward progression, one proceeds through the second rows reached by the clockwise sequence,
starting from the outermost eastern cell and ending at the eighteenth cell, beginning with *ā kā khā*, and so forth.

Likewise, having written the eighteen letters beginning with *a* and ending with *kṣa*, starting from the innermost square and proceeding clockwise from *da* to *kṣa*; and having written the eighteen letters of the third row beginning with *ki, khi, gi*, etc., in the order described, starting from the inside with *di, dhi*, and so on, up to *kā, ni, li, kṣi*.

Having thus written these nineteen syllables in a descending order of exit up to the end of the nineteenth square, [one should place] the fourth vowel together with all its associated consonants in the fourth row and the subsequent remaining rows,
followed by the fifth vowel together with all its associated consonants, and the sixth vowel together with all its associated consonants.

The seventh vowel conjoined with all consonants; the eighth vowel conjoined with all consonants conjoined with that [seventh]; the ninth vowel conjoined with all consonants conjoined with that [eighth]; the tenth vowel conjoined with all consonants conjoined with that [ninth]; the eleventh [vowel] conjoined with all consonants conjoined with that [tenth].

[The sequence of] all consonants connected with the first vowel, all consonants connected with the second vowel, all consonants connected with the third vowel, all consonants connected with the fourth vowel, all consonants connected with the fifth vowel, and all consonants connected with the sixteenth vowel.
Having divided the thirty-six syllables into two equal parts, one should write the first part by entering from the outermost square up to the eighteenth square, following the path of entry. (p.

Having written the second portion, from the inner square up to the nineteenth square, one should inscribe the mantra *ni ā ī* upon the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This then becomes the wheel of the year numbered three hundred and twenty-three, known as the "Anuloma Outer Encasement" (*anulomabāhyasaṃpuṭa*). However, if within this very wheel, from the interior...
Having written the eighteen previously mentioned syllables within the eighteen squares in a clockwise direction (nirgama-gati),
and having written the nineteen syllables beginning with *da* and ending with *kṣa* on the outside in a counter-clockwise direction (praveśa-gati),
one should inscribe the three-syllable mantra *nī dā ī* in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This is then known as the "inner encapsulation in direct order" (*anuloma-abhyantara-sampuṭa*).

The twenty-fourth wheel, consisting of three hundred [squares], is as follows: if, within this very wheel, one begins from the eighteenth square starting from the beginning with the eighteen syllables *a, ka, kha, ga*, and so forth, and writes them in an outward-moving sequence across all eighteen squares ending at the outermost square;

Starting from the nineteenth square and proceeding inward until the innermost square, one should write the letters ending with *a* according to the method of entry described above. Likewise, in the other rows, one should write the second vowel and so forth, along with the consonants corresponding to each respective vowel. In the pericarp (*karṇikā*), however, one should write *nu*, *thā*, and *ī*.
This, then, is the twenty-fifth year-cycle, consisting of three hundred [days], known as the "Reversal of the Outward-Flowing Consonants.
Now, if within this very cycle one proceeds by way of entry through the eighteen squares of the innermost perimeter, beginning from the twenty-first square;

Having written the eighteen letters beginning with *a* and ending with *kṣa*, one should write the letters beginning with *da* and ending with *kṣa* starting from the eighteenth square up to the outermost square.

Having written the second and subsequent vowels along with their corresponding consonants even in the other rows, one should inscribe the three-syllable Vidyā—*nū kṣā ī*—in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This constitutes the wheel of the year numbered thirty-six hundred and twenty-six, known as "the inward reversal in direct order. If, however, in this wheel, [one begins] in the first [square] and the thirty-sixth...

In the second [chapter], the twenty-fifth; in the third, the thirty-fourth; in the fourth, the thirty-third; in the fifth, the thirty-second; in the sixth, the thirty-first; in the thirteenth, the twenty-fourth;
in the fourteenth, the twenty-third; in the fifteenth, the twenty-second; and in the sixteenth, the twenty-first.

In the seventeenth, twentieth, eighteenth, and nineteenth squares, having inscribed in sequence the phonemes of the *tattvas*— taken according to the order and reverse order mentioned in the verse beginning with "dakṣakalakahe"— the three-syllabled *vidyā*, *na ā ī*, is written in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).
Thus, this is the twenty-seventh year-cycle, consisting of two hundred and thirty-seven [units], known as the "Anuloma," "Vāhya," and "Vyākīrṇa. However,

if one calculates by the movement of entry starting from the cell of the leading wind (*agravāta*) within this very cycle— following the method applied throughout this entire section— it is then the thirty-sixth [unit] from that point.
Then, in the first [row], followed by the thirty-fifth, then the second, and so forth— in this manner,
according to a sequence that is the reverse of the order of the previously mentioned grid— the letters beginning with *da* are written. In the other rows as well,
the letters obtained through the clockwise sequence are written according to the order stated above.

In the pericarp, there is the wheel of the twenty-eighth year plus three hundred for each respective *yuga*, known as the "interiorly interspersed in direct order" (*manulomābhyantaravyākīrṇa*). The same applies to the others as well.
The eight-spoked Kālacakra wheels associated with fifty-six years are to be extracted;
the first syllables, beginning with *nḷ nḹ ne nai* and ending with *ve vai vo vau vaṃ vaḥ*,
are to be written in the pericarp according to the distinction of the years, while the second syllables are to be placed in the front path.

Many [scholars] maintain that the wheels for the three hundred and eighty-four years are extracted as forms consisting of the second vowels connected to the letters situated in the first square. Others, however,
hold that in the eight-cornered Kālacakra wheel previously extracted from the lines, the arrangement of the syllables must be performed in a different manner altogether.

For instance, in this wheel, there exist thirty-six rows (vīthī), each consisting of sixteen squares, arranged one below the other in sequence. Among them, in the first row is the group of sixteen beginning with the first vowel; in the second row is the group of sixteen beginning with *ka*, *kā*, *ki*, *kī*, and so forth.

In the third row: *kha khā khi khī*, and so forth. In the fourth row: *ga gā gi gī*, and so forth. In the fifth row: *gha ghā ghi ghī*, and so forth. In the sixth row: *ṅa ṅā ṅi ṅī*, and so forth. In the seventh row: *ca cā ci cī*, and so forth. In the eighth row: *cha chā chi chī*, and so forth.

On the ninth [tithi], *ja jā ji jī* and so forth; on the tenth, *jha jhā jhi jhī* and so forth; on the eleventh, *ña ñā ñi ñī* and so forth; on the twelfth, *ṭa ṭā ṭi ṭī* and so forth; on the thirteenth, *ṭha ṭhā ṭhi ṭhī* and so forth;
on the fourteenth, *ḍa ḍā ḍi ḍī* and so forth; on the fifteenth, *ḍha ḍhā ḍhi ḍhī* and so forth.

On the sixteenth [path], there are ṇa, ṇā, ṇi, ṇī, and so forth. On the seventeenth, there are ta, tā, ti, tī, and so forth. On the eighteenth path, there are tha, thā, thi, thī, and so forth. On the nineteenth path, there are da, dā, di, dī, and so forth.

In the twentieth row: *dha*, *dhā*, *dhi*, *dhī*, and so forth. In the twenty-first row: *na*, *nā*, *ni*, *nī*, and so forth. In the twenty-second row: *pa*, *pā*, *pi*, *pī*, and so forth. In the twenty-third row: *pha*...

Phā, phi, phī, and so forth; in the twenty-fourth row, va, vā, vi, vī, and so forth; in the twenty-fifth row, bha, bhā, bhi, bhī, and so forth; in the twenty-sixth row, ma, mā, mi, mī, and so forth; in the twenty-seventh row, ya, yā, yi, yī, and so forth.

In the twenty-eighth row: *ra rā ri rī*, and so forth. In the twenty-ninth row: *la lā li lī*, and so forth. In the thirtieth row: *va vā vi vī*, and so forth. In the thirty-first row: *śa śā śi śī*, and so forth. In the thirty-second row: *ṣa ṣā ṣi ṣī*, and so forth. In the thirty-third row: [and so forth].
One should write "sa sā si sī" and so forth; in the thirty-fourth row, "ha hā hi hī" and so forth;

in the thirty-fifth row, "la lā li lī"; and in the thirty-sixth row, "kṣa kṣā kṣi kṣī" and so forth—having thus written these sixteen [syllables], one should inscribe the three-syllable mantra "na ā ī" in the pericarp.
This aforementioned first-year wheel of the eight-cornered wheel, known as *anuloma*, becomes the twenty-first year wheel of that cycle [of sixty years] plus three hundred.
Here, by the term "outer square," one's own front square is meant; and by the term "inner square,"...

The sixteenth square situated in that row, starting from the outermost square, is thus described. This is the technical terminology for the eight-cornered (*aṣṭakoṇa*) yantra here. Therefore, in this [yantra], the distinction between the circles and so forth consists solely of the arrangement of lines, not of the placement of letters.
However, if in this very wheel, on the front path (*agravīthī*)...
In the internal grid-positions, beginning from the sixteenth square, the vowels starting with *a* and ending with the *visarjanīya* are written. (p.
In the thirty-two subsequent rows beginning with the second as well, the sixteen forms of each of the thirty-five syllables representing the principles (tattvas) from *ka* to *kṣa* are written,
starting from the sixteenth square designated by the inner cell; thus, *nā*, *ā*, and *ī* are written in the pericarp (*karṇikā*).

Thus, this [wheel] called "forward and reverse" (anuloma-viloma) is the twenty-second wheel of the year within the eight-cornered Wheel of Time (kālacakra); however, for the Wheel of Time beginning with the respective Yugas and so forth, it is the twenty-second wheel of the year plus twenty.
But if, as previously stated, it is indeed in the line-drawn wheel (rekhāmaya-cakra)—
Beginning from the outermost corner cell and proceeding sequentially through the eight cells situated along each respective row until their end,

one should write the thirty-six primary forms of the syllables of the principles (tattvas), beginning with the letter 'A'. Then, starting from each of those respective corner cells, one should proceed toward the sixteenth cell designated as the innermost square.

The second-by-second forms, numbering eight each—beginning with *ḷ*, *ḹ*, *khḷ*, *gḷ*, and so forth, and ending with *hḷ*, *lḷ*, *kṣḷ*—are written in sequence. Within the pericarp are *ni*, *ā*, and *ī*;
this constitutes the eight-spoked wheel known as the "consonant-vowel enclosure" (*saṃpuṭa*) proceeding in direct order (*anuloma*).
Regarding the wheel of the third year, which is the Kālacakra of the respective Yuga and so forth, it constitutes the twenty-third cycle (Kālacakra) out of three hundred and twenty-three.

Furthermore, within this very wheel, from the central line (*agrā*) to the outer paths (*vīthī*), extending as far as the innermost square (*sarvābhyantarakoṣṭha*) according to the previously stated characteristics, there are the first eight forms beginning with *a*, *ka*, *kha*, *ga*, and so on.

Having written all the syllables of reality— starting from the outermost square and extending to the eighth square in each direction— the second forms such as *ḷ*, *kḷ*, *khḷ*, *gḷ*, and so forth, one should inscribe the three-syllable vidyā, namely *nī ā ī*, in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This is the internal [arrangement] in direct order (*anuloma*).

The fourth-year wheel of the eight-spoked wheel called *saṃpuṭa* becomes the twenty-fourth year wheel— counting three hundred [years] plus one— of the respective Kālacakra of the Yugas and so forth. If, however, it is within this very wheel...

Having written the eight vowels beginning with *a* and ending with the left nostril (*vāmanāsā*)— starting from the eighth square of the outermost row and proceeding through the squares in that same horizontal row until the end of the outermost square.
Starting from the ninth square and proceeding in a clockwise direction, one should write the eight vowels beginning with *a* (the first vowel) and ending with *visarga*.
In the very same manner, in the rows running downwards, starting from the eighth vowel and ending at the outermost square, one should write:
*ka kā ki kī*, and so on; *ga gā gi gī*, and so on; *ha hā hi hī*, and so on; *la lā li lī*, and so on; up to *kṣa kṣā kṣi*.
Having written "kṣī" and so forth, and then again starting from the ninth square up to the sixteenth square,
having written "kḷ kḹ ke kai" and so forth, "khḷ khḹ khe khai" and so forth, "gḷ gḹ ge gai" and so forth, "hḷ hḹ he hai" and so forth,
"lḷ lḹ le lai" and so forth, and "kṣḷ kṣḹ kṣe kṣai" and so forth, one should then place the three-syllable mantra "ā ī" in the pericarp (karṇikā).

One should inscribe the Vidyā. This is the wheel of the fifth year for the eight-spoked wheel known as Anuloma-vāhya-parāvṛtta; however, for the wheel of the respective Yugādis, it is the wheel of the twenty-fifth hundredth and thirtieth year.
If, indeed, within this very wheel—

Starting from the ninth square up to the end of the squares located in the horizontal rows of each respective path within the sixteen squares forming the innermost enclosure, one should write the squares beginning with the first vowel; then,
turning back, starting from the eighth square up to the first square which constitutes the outermost enclosure.

Having written the second group of eight [letters] starting from *svara* (the vowels), one proceeds in the same manner through the subsequent rows arranged in descending order, beginning from the ninth cell of the previous [row].

Again, turning back and starting from the eighth square, having written the first group of eight and the second group of eight in sequence, one should inscribe the three-syllabled Vidyā— *nū ā ī*— in the pericarp.
This is the wheel of the sixth year of the eight-spoked wheel, known as the "reversal by inward progression."
In the wheel of the time-cycle (*kālacakra*) of the respective yugas and so forth, there occurs the twenty-sixth cycle of years plus three hundred.

In this very wheel, the letter *a* is in the first square; the letter *a* is in the sixteenth square situated in the horizontal row of that same path; the letter *i* is in the second [square]; and the letter *u* is in the third.

Having written the letter *ū* in the fourteenth [square], *ṛ* in the fourth, *ṝ* in the thirteenth, *ḷ* in the fifth, *ḹ* in the twelfth, *e* in the sixth, *ai* in the eleventh, *oṃ* in the seventh, *au* in the tenth, *aṃ* in the eighth, and *aḥ* in the ninth; one should also write *ka*, *kā*, *ki*, and so forth in the other rows.

Having written the thirty-five syllables beginning with *kī* and the sixteen [syllables] in the pericarp as *nṛ ā ī*, this is the wheel of the seventh year for the eight-cornered wheel known as the "Anuloma," "External," and "Interspersed.
For the Kālacakra of the various Yugas and so forth, however, it constitutes the twenty-seventh wheel plus three hundred. If, moreover, in that very same...

In all thirty-six transverse paths (*tiryag-vīthī*), there are sixteen forms for each of the thirty-six *tattva*-syllables. In the first [set], there are fifteen; in the second, which is reckoned as a fortnight (*pakṣa*), there are fourteen; in the third, they are measured by the Vedas (fourteen); in the fourth, they are measured by the sky (zero); in the fifth, they are measured by the arrows (five); and thereafter, in the sixth, they belong to Śiva (eleven).

Having written [the letters] in the tenth, seventh, and then the ninth *kuñjara* (square), one should write "nṛ" and "ā ī" in the pericarp (*karṇikā*). This is the eight-spoked wheel known as the *manuloma-abhyantaravyākīrṇa*; it constitutes the wheel for the twenty-eighth year plus three hundred [years] of each respective *yuga*. Other [wheels] are likewise [to be constructed].
p.
40a) One should rotate the eight corner wheels of the Kālacakra associated with these fifty-six years following the [initial] eight years.
Therein, in the pericarp (karṇikā), according to the sequence of the years, are the syllables beginning with *nṛ* and ending with *vaṃ vaḥ*: *nṛ*, *nḷ*, *ne*, *nai*, *ve*, *vau*, *vaṃ*, *vaḥ*.

Regarding the four groups consisting of *pa*, *pha*, and *va*, there are fifty-six letters as the first [set], while the second [set] is like the wheels beginning with the *vṛtta*. However, they say that regarding the third letter, there is no dispute for anyone.
The hexagon (*ṣaṭkoṇaka*) has also been essentially extracted. Therein, in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), of the four [letters] consisting of *bha* and *ma*—

For each of the groups (*varga*), sixteen forms [of the letters] are to be presented one by one every year; having first placed [the letters] in order within each single group, the second and subsequent syllables, as well as the eight corners beginning with the *vṛtta*, are to be arranged like the other wheels. Thus, for the four groups, these are to be completed with sixty-four syllables; however, regarding the six-cornered wheel, it is indeed a six-cornered wheel.

Sixty-four years, having been combined, reach their full completion; these are the forty-eight hundred and forty-four (4,484) years required to complete the sixty-four ages of each [cycle], corresponding to the number of years in the six-cornered wheel (*ṣaṭkoṇacakra*). And the square [mandala].

Having marked four equally spaced points in the four directions upon the pericarp of the initial circle, and having completed the four lines by drawing them from point to point, the squares should be filled in all variations according to the method described for the wheel; however, in the pericarp—
The first letters of each of the four groups consisting of *la*, *va*, *ṣa*, and *śa* are obtained in sequence;

thus, with the completion of sixty-four years, twelve hundred and five (1,205) years have passed in total for that particular yuga. The triangular wheel (*trikoṇaka-cakra*) has also been largely extracted. Therein, in the pericarp (*karṇikā*),...

Having first presented, in successive order one by one each year, sixteen forms for each of the four groups consisting of a hundred thousand [mantras], starting with the second and subsequent syllables... (p. 40b)
These are to be worshipped just like the other internal wheels, such as the circles (vṛtta) and so forth, which exceed the eight corners.
Thus, having completed sixty-four years by means of the sixty-four syllables belonging to the four groups, five hundred and seventy-six years of each respective yuga have elapsed. It is thus:
By means of great showers of arrows numbering six and five, the wheels beginning with the nivṛtti-wheel become complete, their number being nine.
On the day this manual was commenced— the same day as the commencement of the *Sudarśana* treatise—

three thousand seventy-two great years (*mahāvarṣa*), composed of *sāvana* days numbered by the "tastes, mountains, and arrows" (676), have elapsed since the beginning of the Kali Yuga. And within those years, the [astronomical] revolutions and so forth have been stated.

The ninefold wheel has passed beyond the wheel of the vowels. And in the sixth cycle, consisting of the ninefold sequence beginning with the *vṛtta* (round) and so forth, the three *Kālacakra*s—namely, the *vṛttacakra*, the thirty-six-cornered *cakra*, and the eighteen-cornered *cakra*—each completed over sixty-four great years, have passed. Now...
The first annual wheel, known as *anuloma*, belongs to the fourth twelve-spoked wheel.

This wheel of seventy-three thousand years is calculated from the beginning of the *yuga*. Here, in the pericarp (*karṇikā*), the first letters appear in sequence: *ṭha, ṭhā, ṭhi, ṭhī, ṭhu, ṭhū*, and so forth; [followed by] *ṇe, ṇai, ṇo, ṇau, ṇaṃ, ṇa*.

Thus, these sixty-four syllables, which arrive in the sequence of their respective years, are to be written in order upon the pericarp for the sixty-four years, beginning with the first syllable. Regarding the second and subsequent syllables, however, there is no difference whatsoever from the Kālacakra [diagram] excluding the circle and the eight corners; thus they have been extracted.

The cycles of the wheel of time, beginning with the commencement of the Yugas and their transitions; among these, the calculation of the specific times attained for each year has been correctly explained above the very subtle layer [of the text]. (p.
Having fashioned eight-petaled lotuses, each with a pericarp adorned by a curved line and an outer circle corresponding in number to the petals,
one should inscribe the mantras of the eight goddesses beginning with Vaśinī on those petals, starting from the eastern petal; this is the method for the installation.

Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* (consecration of the vital breaths) for the yantra according to the aforementioned method, one should worship the goddess Śīlalitā therein. The procedure for this is as follows:

having obtained the *nityavidyā* of the respective cycle, one should join it with the *nityāvidyā* of that specific day, repeating the three-syllable mantra twice, and then sequentially employ the six *jāti-mantras* beginning with "to the Heart, *namaḥ*," and so forth.

Having performed the six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) on the thumbs and other fingers, as well as on the heart and other body parts, and having performed the installation using the daily mantra together with the six-limbed mantra, one should worship the deities of the previously mentioned pedestal at the conclusion of the primary ritual resolve; then, one should worship the principal Goddess in the pericarp and her attendants from behind her.
Having worshipped the weapons on the left and right sides, and having worshipped the eight divine ones on the petals,

one should worship with the respective mantras as stated in the section on the Full Consecration (*pūrṇābhiṣeka*), in such forms as: *hrīṃ śrīṃ a ā ī rūpaśaktipādukāṃ pūjayāmi*, *hrīṃ śrīṃ akā ī rūpaśaktipādukāṃ pūjayāmi*, and so forth.
One should recite the Kalanityā-vidyās, numbering twenty-seven hundred and thirty-six.

Having extracted the Śrīcakra by first arranging the *bindus* within all [the triangles], such that they fall inside each respective syllable and *bindu*— including the names of the practitioner (*sādhaka*) and the object of practice (*sādhya*) written upon the pericarp (*karṇikā*)— which are obtained in their respective years of application according to the previously mentioned Kālacakra; therein...

Having first performed the worship of the Devīpīṭha and having worshipped the nine enclosures (navāvaraṇa) as before, one should worship the seventy-six and five hundred [deities]— the powers (śaktis) whose colors correspond to the written syllables of their respective wheels (cakras)— with mantras beginning with "I worship the sandals (pādukā) of Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aśakti," and so forth.

Having worshipped the eight goddesses of speech, such as Vaśinī and the others, who are drawn upon the eight petals outside the entire circle, one should complete the remainder of the worship as before.
By that, the practitioner attains all his desires and gains power that is unimpeded in every respect.
Having consecrated the previously mentioned Śrīcakra situated within the Kālacakra according to the aforementioned ritual,
and having seated therein a woman of beautiful ruddy complexion endowed with the full bloom of youth,

one should perform the worship of the deities of the seats (*pīṭhadevatā*) preceded by the ritual for attaining the power of command (*ājñāśakti*), as described in the method for when the sun has entered the zodiac sign of Pisces (*mīnarāśi*).

For the practitioner who worships every year on the full moon day (pūrṇimā), the Goddess Śrī Lalitā will certainly become pleased, even if there should arise some mental agitation of desire through the touch or sight of the performance of worship and so forth. Thus are two applications that accomplish all desired goals. The extraction of the Śrīcakra is as follows: beginning with one hand...
Having established a square of equal lines with the prescribed length and breadth,
one should drop the Brahma-sūtra (the central north-south axis) through the middle of the east-west line, ensuring it touches the center of the respective east-west sides of that square.
Then, having divided [the area] into six parts, at the end of the eighth portion on each side within the square, [one should mark] the previous east-west line.

Having fashioned a second square by expanding the four touched lines, one should begin from the center of the horizontal line situated in the northern portion of the divider of the northwest corner-cell—

which lies between the two squares and within the space of eight parts along the eastern and western paths of those two squares— starting from the middle of the horizontal line located in the northern part that divides the northwest corner cell.
Having laid down a single thread extending from east to west, reaching as far as the center of the horizontal line situated within the divider of the Īśāna (northeast) square;
then, starting from the center of the horizontal line located in the eastern portion of the divider of the Nairṛtya (southwest) corner square.
Having laid down another thread extending from east to west, reaching to the center, along the horizontal line at the end of the division of the fire-compartment (vahnikoṣṭha).

Having laid down diagonal threads in each of the compartments at the northeast and southwest corners, starting from their respective southeast points and ending at their respective northwest points; and having laid down threads in each of the compartments at the northwest and southeast corners, starting from their respective northeast points and ending at their respective southwest points— thereby forming eight compartments in total— one prepares the square path (vīthī).
Having drawn two intersecting lines and thus formed two doors,
one should erase the internal square-line connected to those door-lines at both doors,
and also erase each of the two lines within the doors that are related to the *brahmasūtra*.
The first of the nine wheels that constitute the Śrīcakra is a square wheel with eighteen compartments, possessing two gates and extending outward on all sides. Then,
occupying the central position of the Brahma-thread by means of forty squares according to the Brahma-thread of Vasiṣṭha—

Having formed a circle consisting of the tips of sixteen petals by rotating a compass whose leg touches and does not touch the lines within the square; then, having formed the circle of the filaments by rotating [the compass] thirty-four degrees within that, and the circle of the sixteen petals by rotating it thirty degrees from the circle of the filaments; there, at the tip—

At the point where the two Brahma-threads intersect, having marked twelve points at equal intervals around that very circle in the four directions— east, west, north, and south— and having established all [the lines] within the innermost [circle],
[the circle] is divided into six parts.
Having established four marks by taking a measurement of three parts on each side from both sides of the intersection of the Brahma-line and the diameter-line,
and having fashioned sixteen petals by drawing thirty-two lines with equal intervals between them;
